statement: A full root-cause review is compulsory following every minor security event, regardless of relevance or feasibility.
norm_summary: Post-incident review is called for where appropriate after recovery; where possible it should identify causes and lead to documented lessons for prevention and impact reduction.
diagnostic_note: The false statement removes conditional wording and expands incidents to all minor events.

statement: Previous significant cybersecurity incidents need not be considered when choosing how to assess security-control effectiveness.
norm_summary: Processes for effectiveness assessment account for risk-assessment results and past significant incidents and specify what to measure, how, when and by whom.
diagnostic_note: The false statement removes an explicitly required input.

statement: An internal independent review can be performed by qualified internal staff if they are not in the reporting chain of the audited area.
norm_summary: Independent information-security reviews must be done by audit-competent people; internal reviewers must be outside the reporting authority of personnel in the area being assessed.

statement: The incident-handling policy only needs to describe how to notify the authorities; internal detection and recovery procedures are optional.
norm_summary: An incident-handling policy must allocate responsibilities and establish procedures for detection, analysis, containment or response, recovery, documentation and timely incident reporting.
diagnostic_note: The false statement omits mandatory internal lifecycle elements.

statement: Risk assessment outputs and treatment plans are revisited at least annually and following significant incidents or major risk changes.
norm_summary: Risk assessment results and risk treatment plans are reviewed at planned intervals, at least annually, and after significant incidents or changes in operations or risks.

statement: Effectiveness-assessment procedures account for relevant risk assessments and previous significant incidents, specifying measurement responsibilities.
norm_summary: Processes for effectiveness assessment account for risk-assessment results and past significant incidents and specify what to measure, how, when and by whom.

statement: Residual cybersecurity risks may be accepted by any project team member without management reporting.
norm_summary: Entities must document risk assessments, implement a treatment plan and obtain acceptance of assessments and residual risks from management or properly authorised accountable persons, with management reporting.
diagnostic_note: The false statement removes risk authority and reporting safeguards.

statement: The default legal requirement is to provide all staff with broad privileged access until a misuse occurs.
norm_summary: The management of access rights must reflect the principles of need-to-know, least privilege and separation of duties.
diagnostic_note: The false statement contradicts least privilege and need-to-know.

statement: An internal department manager is always permitted to independently review their own directly reporting team.
norm_summary: Independent information-security reviews must be done by audit-competent people; internal reviewers must be outside the reporting authority of personnel in the area being assessed.
diagnostic_note: The false statement contradicts the independence safeguard for internal reviewers.

statement: Backup integrity checks are unnecessary as long as the backups are stored off-site.
norm_summary: Relevant entities must check backup-copy integrity regularly.
diagnostic_note: The false statement invents an exemption unsupported by the provision.

statement: The entity carries out regular integrity checks of its backup copies.
norm_summary: Relevant entities must check backup-copy integrity regularly.

statement: If an emergency bypasses routine change procedures, the organisation documents what changed and why the usual process could not be used.
norm_summary: When emergency changes cannot follow ordinary change procedures, the entity must document the change result and why normal procedures were not followed.

statement: The incident-handling policy should cover response roles and processes including detection, containment, recovery and timely reporting.
norm_summary: An incident-handling policy must allocate responsibilities and establish procedures for detection, analysis, containment or response, recovery, documentation and timely incident reporting.

statement: Cybersecurity training is only necessary for newly hired personnel and may never be required when someone changes roles.
norm_summary: Staff who move into positions requiring security-relevant competencies and expertise must receive corresponding training.
diagnostic_note: The false statement wrongly excludes role-change training.

statement: Residual cybersecurity risks can be accepted by accountable, authorised risk owners where the management body receives adequate reporting.
norm_summary: Entities must document risk assessments, implement a treatment plan and obtain acceptance of assessments and residual risks from management or properly authorised accountable persons, with management reporting.

statement: Emergency changes are exempt from all post-change documentation because normal approval steps may be bypassed.
norm_summary: When emergency changes cannot follow ordinary change procedures, the entity must document the change result and why normal procedures were not followed.
diagnostic_note: The false statement treats exceptional process bypass as permission to omit required documentation.

statement: An entity assigns at least one person to report directly to its management body on network and information security matters.
norm_summary: At least one person is required to report directly to the management body about network and information system security.

statement: All incident response procedures must be tested once every 24 hours under the implementing regulation.
norm_summary: The entity must test its incident response procedures at planned intervals; a fixed daily testing schedule is not prescribed in this point.
diagnostic_note: The false statement invents a daily frequency absent from the point.

statement: Where feasible and necessary for the role, entities verify the backgrounds of employees and applicable direct suppliers or service providers.
norm_summary: Background verification is ensured to the extent feasible for employees and, where applicable, direct suppliers and service providers, when necessary for their roles, responsibilities and authorisations.

statement: Every employee working in IT security must report directly to the management body on security matters.
norm_summary: At least one person is required to report directly to the management body about network and information system security.
diagnostic_note: The false statement generalises a minimum-one-person reporting line to every security worker.

statement: Every relevant entity must maintain a fuel-powered emergency generator regardless of its risk exposure or operational circumstances.
norm_summary: The listed protections against supporting utility disruption are applied where appropriate; examples include backup utilities and other safeguards.
diagnostic_note: The false statement turns an illustrative conditional utility safeguard into a universal generator requirement.

statement: Every employee and every subcontractor must undergo identical background checks irrespective of feasibility, role or applicable conditions.
norm_summary: Background verification is ensured to the extent feasible for employees and, where applicable, direct suppliers and service providers, when necessary for their roles, responsibilities and authorisations.
diagnostic_note: The false statement removes feasibility, applicability and role-based conditions.

statement: The organisation maintains an up-to-date list of its direct suppliers and services, including contact information and the relevant ICT offerings.
norm_summary: A current registry of direct suppliers and service providers is required, including contact points and the ICT products, services and processes they provide.

statement: The organisation must record the identity of every indirect subcontractor of every supplier, without exception, in the prescribed supplier register.
norm_summary: A current registry of direct suppliers and service providers is required, including contact points and the ICT products, services and processes they provide.
diagnostic_note: The false statement expands the statutory direct-supplier registry into an absolute register of all indirect subcontractors.

statement: Secure development rules are mandated only for the final testing stage; requirements and architecture stages are outside scope.
norm_summary: Rules for secure software and systems development apply to in-house and outsourced development, covering specification, design, development, implementation and testing.
diagnostic_note: The false statement deletes the earlier phases from lifecycle coverage.

statement: The network and information security policy is only required to be reviewed once every five years, even after significant incidents.
norm_summary: The NIS security policy must be reviewed by management at least annually and after major incidents or material operational or risk changes; update as appropriate and document the review.
diagnostic_note: The false assertion replaces the annual and event-driven review requirement with a five-year interval.

statement: Training must cover employees transferring to roles that require cybersecurity-relevant expertise.
norm_summary: Staff who move into positions requiring security-relevant competencies and expertise must receive corresponding training.

statement: The regulation requires a risk assessment refresh only when an entity first enters the scope of the regulation.
norm_summary: Risk assessment results and risk treatment plans are reviewed at planned intervals, at least annually, and after significant incidents or changes in operations or risks.
diagnostic_note: The false statement omits recurring and event-driven reviews.

statement: Where appropriate, users authenticate with multiple factors or continuous mechanisms taking the classification of the accessed asset into account.
norm_summary: Multi-factor or continuous authentication is applied where appropriate for access to the network and information systems, considering asset classification.

statement: The regulation mandates AES-256 encryption for every dataset, device and communication channel without regard to classification or risk.
norm_summary: Entities need a cryptography policy and procedures aligned to asset classification and risk assessment to protect confidentiality, authenticity and integrity.
diagnostic_note: The false statement invents an algorithm and removes the risk/asset-based approach.

statement: Incident response procedures must be tested at defined, planned intervals.
norm_summary: The entity must test its incident response procedures at planned intervals; a fixed daily testing schedule is not prescribed in this point.

statement: The choice and use of cryptography should follow the organisation’s asset classification and cybersecurity risk assessment.
norm_summary: Entities need a cryptography policy and procedures aligned to asset classification and risk assessment to protect confidentiality, authenticity and integrity.

statement: Where appropriate, the entity conducts post-incident reviews after recovery and documents lessons learned to reduce future incident impact.
norm_summary: Post-incident review is called for where appropriate after recovery; where possible it should identify causes and lead to documented lessons for prevention and impact reduction.

statement: Secure development rules apply throughout the development lifecycle, including systems built internally or by outsourced teams.
norm_summary: Rules for secure software and systems development apply to in-house and outsourced development, covering specification, design, development, implementation and testing.

statement: Every discovered vulnerability, irrespective of criticality, must be completely remediated within exactly 24 hours.
norm_summary: The vulnerability-handling measures include addressing vulnerabilities identified as critical to operations without undue delay; no universal 24-hour deadline is imposed here.
diagnostic_note: The false statement imposes a fixed deadline and generalises critical vulnerabilities to every finding.

statement: Entities implement suitable utility-resilience safeguards, as appropriate, to address risks from electricity, telecommunications or other utilities.
norm_summary: The listed protections against supporting utility disruption are applied where appropriate; examples include backup utilities and other safeguards.

statement: The management body reviews the network and information security policy at least once per year and upon significant incidents or changes, recording the review outcome.
norm_summary: The NIS security policy must be reviewed by management at least annually and after major incidents or material operational or risk changes; update as appropriate and document the review.

statement: Every login to every information system must always use exactly two authentication factors, with no asset-based exceptions.
norm_summary: Multi-factor or continuous authentication is applied where appropriate for access to the network and information systems, considering asset classification.
diagnostic_note: The false statement removes the where-appropriate condition and substitutes an unconditional exactly-two-factors rule.

statement: Vulnerabilities identified as critical for operations must be addressed without undue delay.
norm_summary: The vulnerability-handling measures include addressing vulnerabilities identified as critical to operations without undue delay; no universal 24-hour deadline is imposed here.

statement: Access grants and revocations follow least privilege, need-to-know and segregation of duties.
norm_summary: The management of access rights must reflect the principles of need-to-know, least privilege and separation of duties.
